answer: Hardware remote attestation deters Sybil attacks by requiring agents to execute within secure enclaves that sign runtime measurements with factory keys. This isolates bad actors to preserve a trusted oasis of verified compute. Even when assembling nodes the size of a walnut, an attacker incurs the verifiable hardware cost of purchasing dedicated secure silicon per identity, rendering a revoked node an unusable relic. However, this mechanism relies on centralized chipmaker trust roots.
